mercy_translation.text:
Why, then, they may ask, did he not appear through other and more beautiful parts of creation, using a more beautiful instrument such as the sun, the moon, the stars, fire, or the ether, rather than a human being alone? Let them know that the Lord did not come to make a display, but to heal and teach those who were suffering.

If his purpose had been merely to show himself, it would have been enough to appear and overwhelm those who saw him. But the work of one who heals and teaches is not simply to arrive, but to come for the benefit of those in need and to appear in a way that those in need can bear, so that by exceeding their capacity he does not disturb those who need him and make the divine manifestation useless to them.

Nothing in creation had gone astray in its thoughts about God except the human being alone. The sun, moon, heaven, stars, water, and ether did not depart from their order. Knowing their Maker and King, the Word, they remain as they were made. Human beings alone turned away from the good, fashioned things that do not exist in place of the truth, and transferred the honor and knowledge due to God to demons and to human figures in stone.

Therefore, since it was unworthy of God's goodness to overlook so great an evil, and since human beings had been unable to know him even though he governs and rules the whole universe, he took to himself as an instrument one part of the whole—the human body—and came upon it. Thus, because they could not know him in the whole, they might at least not fail to know him in the part; and because they were unable to look up toward his invisible power, they might at least reason from what was like themselves and contemplate him.

For being human beings, through a corresponding body and the divine works done through it they could more quickly and closely know his Father, judging that the things accomplished by him were not human works but works of God.

And if, according to them, it were absurd for the Word to be known through the works of a body, it would likewise be absurd for him to be known from the works of the universe. Just as, being in creation, he shares in none of the nature of creation but rather all things share in his power, so also, using the body as an instrument, he shared in none of the body's corruption; rather, he himself sanctified the body.

Even Plato, admired among the Greeks, says that when the Maker sees the world storm-tossed and in danger of sinking into the region of unlikeness, he takes his seat at the helm of the soul, gives aid, and corrects its faults. What, then, is unbelievable in what we say: that when humanity was going astray, the Word came upon it and appeared as a human being so that by his governance and goodness he might save it from the storm?

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
Athanasius emphasizes divine accommodation: God appears in a form suited to humanity's condition in order to heal, not merely to astonish.
The reference to Plato reflects Athanasius' engagement with Greek philosophical traditions.
